forecast-period.text: A trough and cold front moved across SA early on Saturday and will continue to move away to the east overnight. A ridge of high pressure will follow and move over SA overnight and on Sunday. Another cold front will move across southern coasts early Monday but the ridge will persist further north. A trough over the interior of WA will be near stationary early to mid next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning fog about western and central parts. Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural areas. Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west in the afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures above average in the far northwest but below average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds, tending east to northeasterly in the far west.

Gusty showers and thunderstorms about the southern agricultural area, contracting to the southeast during the afternoon. Thunderstorms may be severe about the Lower South East with the risk of damaging wind gusts. Fresh to strong and gusty west to southwesterly winds, tending southwest to southeasterly in the west and north.

Patchy morning fog about central and eastern parts. Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural area, clearing late afternoon. Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures mostly below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty about northern parts during the day, tending east to northeasterly in the west.

text.p: Morning fog patches about the agricultural areas and possible early frost about the South East districts. Dry apart from showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh near western coasts during the afternoon, tending east to northeasterly in the west.
Dry apart from showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: 2 to 5 mm about the southern agricultural area and less than 2 mm about the northern agricultural area. 5 to 15 mm is possible in the far west, west of about Ceduna, but local heavier falls of 20 to 40 mm are possible nearer the western border with thunderstorms.
